title: One pipeline per item type
statement: Generate each item type through its own steps and its own checks, so that a change to one type cannot break another.
detail: A synthesis across five corpora of the AP work marks per-type generation as confirmed in four of them and notes that two generators improved when their validators became type-specific (`MASTER_SYNTHESIS.md`, lines 74 and 259). One generator's report makes per-type modules a first rule, with no single prompt shared by every item type, so that one type can change without risking another (`ap_social_studies_generator_distilled.md`, lines 54 and 172). Another lists the type-specific checks to run before scoring: option count, answer count, explanation consistency, answer uniqueness and schema validity (`k_12_social_studies_distilled.md`, line 74).
against: No source compares per-type and shared generation head to head: the synthesis tallies where the pattern was confirmed rather than measuring it (`MASTER_SYNTHESIS.md`, line 74).

evidence.quote: | Per-type generation | confirmed | confirmed | confirmed | confirmed | compatible | T1 |
- Use per-type generator modules. APUSH production should not have one shared prompt surface for all cells.
- This is the right ownership boundary: change MCQ_SET without risking DBQ or SAQ.
- Add type-specific deterministic validators before scoring: option count, answer count, explanation consistency, answer uniqueness, schema validity.
- K-12 and AP generator both improved when validators became type-specific.
